source.title: Identifying Functionally Important Features with End-to-End Sparse Dictionary Learning

record.file_problem: The Alignment Forum text is explicitly a short summary of the paper; the underlying paper and its full figures are not included.
record.tranche_reason: Reports SAE feature-representation results on GPT2-small and Tinystories-1M, extending discussion of sparse dictionary features beyond toy models.
record.gate_note: The text reports comparisons of feature counts, output-performance preservation, downstream reconstruction, and feature-direction similarity. It does not report evidence about toy networks, neuron polysemanticity, or feature stability as canonical model units. Exact figure values for several comparisons are not stated in the text.
record.test_reason: A method paper. It trains SAEs on GPT2-small and Tinystories-1M with a new end-to-end KL objective and compares it with standard local SAEs on efficiency, downstream reconstruction and within-dictionary geometry. It assumes models hold sparse features that SAEs can recover. It does not test whether LLMs superpose features (V4) or whether SAE features are canonical units (V5); it only reports its own method against baselines.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that e2e SAEs are a Pareto improvement over local SAEs: more performance explained, fewer total and active features, and no cost to interpretability. The e2e+downstream variant keeps these gains while following computational pathways much closer to the original model. Local SAEs show more feature splitting. The added cost is longer training time.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains SAEs on model activations, using an end-to-end output-distribution KL objective and, in one variant, downstream reconstruction losses. It is not the original toy-network setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reconstruction objective changes downstream pathway similarity and within-dictionary cosine similarity: SAE_e2e differs more from SAE_local than SAE_e2e+downstream does.

fits_no_version.finding: The SAE training objective changes how many features are needed at matched performance explained, and how tightly dictionary directions cluster. Local SAEs show more clustering, a proxy for feature splitting: about 0.04 higher than e2e+ds and 0.166 higher than e2e.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The dictionary an SAE recovers, including its size, sparsity and degree of feature splitting, depends on its training objective rather than being fixed by the model.

record.peer_reviewed: Alignment Forum post; peer-review status not stated
record.problems: The supplied text is a summary rather than the full paper, and several figure results are reported only qualitatively without exact values or model-separated results. The authors also note that SAE_e2e may use a different computational pathway from the original model.
record.rows_left_out: The summary mentions automated interpretability and qualitative analyses, but gives no outcome values or specific result adequate for a separate row. It also mentions longer training time without a stated comparison value.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transitions or geometry of superposition.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity-allocation analysis.
Does not test whether features are spread across neurons. SAE recoverability is assumed, not tested against a baseline.
No cross-seed stability or completeness results in the supplied summary. Only the objective-dependence of dictionaries is shown indirectly.

missing.what: Cross-seed similarity of e2e SAE features. A commenter says the paper claims e2e features differ greatly across seeds, and reports his own Jaccard and decoder-similarity replication. This bears on V5 stability but is not in the supplied summary.
missing.locator: Full paper (arXiv:2405.12241) geometric analysis; Logan Riggs comments

record.verdict_notes: The source is an Alignment Forum summary of the paper, so exact figure values and per-model results are absent. The reader treated method-comparison rows as V4 evidence. I reclassify the study as T4 because it uses SAEs as a tool and reports its own method's performance. Its relevance to V5 (non-canonical, objective- and seed-dependent dictionaries) would need the full paper.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular superposition geometry.
Whether neuron polysemanticity results from competition for capacity, or whether important features get dedicated neurons or dimensions.
Polysemantic neurons arising for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Whether features are spread across neurons; whether the learned dictionary features are the model's natural features rather than features that preserve outputs through another computational pathway.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable across seeds or methods, or canonical units of the model.
Whether the model's underlying features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.
